title: Bakken begins near Copenhagen
description: A spring at Dyrehavsbakken draws crowds and entertainers; it is recognised as the oldest operating amusement park.

title: Promenades Aeriennes opens in Paris
description: Wheeled cars locked to a track with guide rails: the first recognisable roller coaster, inspired by Russian ice slides.

title: Mauch Chunk Switchback Railway built
description: A Pennsylvania coal-hauling gravity railway that later carried tourists for thrills, a model for LaMarcus Thompson.

title: Tivoli Gardens opens in Copenhagen
description: Georg Carstensen's pleasure garden mixes rides, music and lights; Walt Disney later cites it as a model.

title: Mauch Chunk Switchback adds an uphill ratchet
description: The cable-hauled Up Route gets a ratchet so a loose car cannot run back downhill, the ancestor of the anti-rollback device.

title: Pepper's ghost premieres at the Royal Polytechnic
description: John Henry Pepper stages Henry Dircks's angled-glass ghost illusion in London; the pair patent it in 1863.

title: Thompson's Switchback Railway opens at Coney Island
description: A five-cent gravity ride at just over 6 mph, usually dated as America's first purpose-built roller coaster.

title: World's Columbian Exposition opens in Chicago
description: The Midway Plaisance and the 264 ft Ferris Wheel show that amusements can anchor a fair.

title: Sea Lion Park opens at Coney Island
description: Paul Boyton's enclosed park with a single admission gate sets the amusement-park pattern.

title: Blackpool Pleasure Beach founded
description: William George Bean and John Outhwaite start Britain's defining seaside amusement park.

title: Steeplechase Park opens at Coney Island
description: George Tilyou builds a park around his mechanical racing horses, inspired by the Chicago midway.

title: Wiener Riesenrad built at the Prater
description: Vienna's 64.75 m Ferris wheel becomes a permanent landmark of the European fairground.

title: Kennywood opens as a trolley park
description: The Monongahela Street Railway opens a picnic ground at the end of its Pittsburgh line.

title: Leap-The-Dips opens at Lakemont Park
description: A side-friction figure-eight coaster that is now the oldest standing roller coaster in the world.

title: Luna Park opens at Coney Island
description: Thompson and Dundy light 200,000 bulbs over a fantasy city built around A Trip to the Moon.

title: Yerkes and Dodson publish the inverted-U arousal law
description: Their mouse-learning study becomes the basis of the idea that there is an optimal level of arousal.

title: Erlang publishes the first queueing-theory paper
description: Agner Erlang models random telephone calls at the Copenhagen exchange, founding the mathematics later applied to ride queues.

title: John Miller's underfriction wheels
description: Wheels under the rail let coasters take steeper drops and sharper curves, opening the 1920s golden age.

title: John Miller's under-rail roller patent granted
description: US 1,319,888 describes rollers travelling under the rail to stop wheels jumping off the track, the basis of upstop wheels.

title: Liseberg opens in Gothenburg
description: A city-owned park that becomes one of Scandinavia's most visited attractions.

title: Coney Island Cyclone opens
description: Vernon Keenan's wooden coaster survives the Depression and is landmarked in 1988.

title: Knott's Ghost Town opens
description: Walter Knott's replica western town turns a berry stand into a themed destination.

title: Walt Disney founds the company that becomes Walt Disney Imagineering
description: WDI describes itself as founded in 1952, combining design firm, development company, storytelling studio and innovation lab.

title: Efteling's Fairytale Forest opens
description: Anton Pieck's illustrated fairy tales become walk-through scenes; 222,941 visitors in year one.

title: Walt Disney founds the company that becomes Imagineering
description: Set up to design Disneyland; renamed WED Enterprises in 1953 and Walt Disney Imagineering in 1986.

title: Walt Disney forms the company that becomes WED Enterprises
description: A private design unit, renamed WED in 1953 and Walt Disney Imagineering in 1986.

title: Harrison Price's site study picks Anaheim
description: Walt and Roy Disney hire the Stanford Research Institute; economist Harrison "Buzz" Price compares ten Southern California sites and recommends a 160-acre orange grove in Anaheim.

title: Buzz Price's Disneyland site study
description: Economist Harrison Price recommends Anaheim for Disneyland on access, climate and projected profit, the model for park feasibility studies.

title: Disneyland opens
description: A $17 million park with five lands and twenty attractions; the press preview is remembered as Black Sunday.

title: Disneyland opens with the first hub-and-spoke park plan
description: A single entrance, Main Street, a central plaza and lands radiating from it set the template for most later theme parks.

title: Disneyland opens
description: Main Street's forced perspective, the castle weenie, the berm and the Jungle Cruise spiel set the vocabulary of spatial storytelling.

title: Freeman Tilden publishes Interpreting Our Heritage
description: The principles of heritage interpretation that themed design later borrows from museums and national parks.

title: Matterhorn Bobsleds opens
description: Arrow Development builds the first permanent tubular-steel roller coaster.

title: Matterhorn Bobsleds opens with tubular steel track
description: Arrow Development builds the first permanently installed tubular-steel track coaster at Disneyland.

title: Matterhorn Bobsleds opens at Disneyland
description: First permanent tubular-steel roller coaster, built by Arrow Development.

title: Kevin Lynch publishes The Image of the City
description: Names paths, edges, districts, nodes and landmarks as the elements of a legible place; later a staple of park wayfinding.

title: Kevin Lynch publishes The Image of the City
description: Paths, edges, districts, nodes and landmarks become the standard vocabulary for legible places, later borrowed by park planners.

title: Freedomland U.S.A. opens in the Bronx
description: C. V. Wood's map-shaped park opens; it is bankrupt after the 1964 season.

title: Little proves L = λW
description: John Little's Operations Research paper proves the queueing relationship behind every wait-time estimate.

title: Six Flags Over Texas opens
description: Angus Wynne's park starts the regional theme park chain model.

title: Enchanted Tiki Room opens
description: The first attraction to use Audio-Animatronics figures.

title: Enchanted Tiki Room opens at Disneyland
description: First Audio-Animatronics show: roughly 150 birds, flowers and tikis driven from recorded tape.

title: New York World's Fair opens with four Disney shows
description: it's a small world, Mr. Lincoln, Carousel of Progress and the Ford Magic Skyway are funded by sponsors.

title: Universal Studio Tour opens in Hollywood
description: The modern tram tour of a working studio, the seed of Universal's parks.

title: Steeplechase Park closes
description: Coney Island's last great park closes after decades of decline.

title: Walt Disney dies
description: Roy O. Disney postpones retirement to finish the Florida project.

title: Omnimover debuts in Adventure Thru Inner Space
description: A continuous chain of swivelling vehicles that aim riders' eyes; patented 1968.

title: Pirates of the Caribbean opens
description: Planned as a wax museum, it becomes a boat ride; the last attraction Walt worked on.

title: Reedy Creek Improvement District created
description: Florida's governor signs the act giving Disney's Florida resort its own utility, building-code and fire powers.

title: Adventure Thru Inner Space opens
description: First attraction to use Disney's Omnimover continuous-chain vehicle system.

title: Haunted Mansion opens at Disneyland
description: Six years after its facade was finished, the Mansion opens with Doom Buggies and a Pepper's ghost ballroom.

title: The Haunted Mansion opens at Disneyland
description: Its ballroom becomes the most famous Pepper's ghost scene, and filmed faces projected onto busts foreshadow projection mapping.

title: The Haunted Mansion opens at Disneyland
description: Its stretching room becomes the archetypal pre-show and its ballroom the most famous Pepper's ghost.

title: Masahiro Mori describes the uncanny valley
description: Essay in the Japanese journal Energy sketches the dip in affinity for almost-human figures.

title: John Fruin publishes Pedestrian Planning and Design
description: Introduces pedestrian level of service grades based on space per person.

title: Fruin publishes Pedestrian Planning and Design
description: John J. Fruin introduces the pedestrian level-of-service scale used to size walkways and queues.

title: Walt Disney World opens
description: Magic Kingdom and two hotels open on land bought in secret through dummy companies.

title: Magic Kingdom opens above its utilidors
description: Service corridors built at ground level, with the park raised on lagoon fill, keep cast and deliveries out of sight.

title: Kotler names 'atmospherics'
description: Philip Kotler's Journal of Retailing paper argues the sensory design of a space is a marketing tool in its own right.

title: Reason and Brand publish Motion Sickness
description: The monograph sets out sensory conflict theory, still the default explanation for simulator and ride sickness.

title: Appleton publishes The Experience of Landscape
description: Prospect-refuge theory: people prefer places where they can see out while feeling sheltered.

title: Space Mountain opens at Magic Kingdom
description: An indoor coaster in the dark, built with Arrow Development; Disneyland's version follows in 1977.

title: Corkscrew opens at Knott's Berry Farm
description: Arrow's first modern inverting coaster turns riders upside down twice.

title: Europa-Park opens in Rust
description: The Mack family opens a park to show off its rides; it grows to 18 European-themed areas.

title: The Great American Revolution opens
description: Schwarzkopf and Stengel bring back the vertical loop with a clothoid shape.

title: Great American Revolution opens with a clothoid loop
description: Werner Stengel's teardrop loop at Six Flags Magic Mountain makes the first modern vertical loop survivable at 4.9 g.

title: King Kobra opens at Kings Dominion
description: First Schwarzkopf Shuttle Loop, launched by a dropped weight; flywheel launches followed in 1978.

title: ASTM Committee F24 formed
description: ASTM International creates Committee F24 on Amusement Rides and Devices, the home of F2291, F770, F1193 and F2974.

title: Alton Towers opens as a theme park
description: A pay-one-price park with the Corkscrew coaster on a stately-home estate.

title: EPCOT Center opens
description: Walt's city of tomorrow becomes a park of Future World pavilions and World Showcase.

title: Tokyo Disneyland opens
description: The first Disney park abroad, owned by Oriental Land Company under licence.

title: Hillier and Hanson publish The Social Logic of Space
description: The founding text of space syntax, which predicts movement from the shape of a path network.

title: Ulrich's window-view study appears in Science
description: Surgical patients with a view of trees recovered faster than matched patients facing a brick wall.

title: Maister's The Psychology of Waiting Lines appears
description: Eight propositions about perceived waits, published in the collection The Service Encounter.

title: USITT publishes DMX512
description: A single serial standard for lighting control replaces proprietary dimmer protocols; later ANSI E1.11.

title: 'Scent-Emitting Systems' patent granted
description: Robert E. McCarthy's US 4,603,030, filed 20 September 1984, describes the programmable multi-scent dispenser known in Disney parks as the Smellitzer.

title: NAARSO founded
description: The National Association of Amusement Ride Safety Officials begins its inspector certification and safety seminars.

title: Larson's queue-fairness paper in Operations Research
description: Social justice and the psychology of queueing, including the case for serpentine single lines.

title: Magnum XL-200 opens at Cedar Point
description: The first coaster over 200 ft starts the coaster wars.

title: Universal Studios Florida opens
description: Jaws, Kongfrontation and Earthquake break down on opening; Universal issues return vouchers.

title: Universal Studios Florida opens around a lagoon
description: Themed areas arranged around a central lagoon establish the loop layout as the main alternative to the hub.

title: Marty Sklar starts the Imaginations Design Competition
description: Walt Disney Imagineering's student competition launches; many participants later become interns.

title: Riccio and Stoffregen propose postural instability theory
description: An ecological alternative to sensory conflict as the cause of motion sickness.

title: Bitner publishes 'Servicescapes'
description: Journal of Marketing paper linking ambient conditions, layout and signage to customer and employee behaviour.

title: Euro Disney opens
description: Attendance misses targets and debt reaches about $3 billion before a 1994 rescue.

title: Euro Disney opens near Paris
description: Opens with largely American menus and no alcohol in the park; attendance misses forecasts.

title: Batman: The Ride opens
description: B&M's first inverted coaster, later cloned worldwide.

title: Batman: The Ride opens at Six Flags Great America
description: First inverted roller coaster, by Bolliger & Mabillard.

title: Fantasmic! opens at Disneyland
description: Animation projected onto three mist screens, with fire and pyrotechnics, sets the template for water-screen spectaculars.

title: Kahneman and colleagues publish the cold-water peak-end study
description: When More Pain Is Preferred to Less establishes the peak-end rule.

title: Euro Disney begins serving wine and beer with meals
description: Reverses the no-alcohol policy in response to European expectations.

title: First Thea Awards presented
description: TEA holds the first Thea Awards at the Biltmore Hotel in Los Angeles; Harrison 'Buzz' Price receives the first Lifetime Achievement Award.

title: TEA creates the Thea Awards
description: The Themed Entertainment Association starts peer awards for outstanding projects.

title: Marvel and MCA sign the Universal theme-park licence
description: The agreement that still restricts which Marvel characters Disney may use in its U.S. parks.

title: Tower of Terror opens
description: Otis-built cabs are pulled down faster than gravity at Disney-MGM Studios.

title: Social force model published
description: Helbing and Molnar's pedestrian model in Physical Review E becomes the basis of agent-based crowd simulation.

title: Indiana Jones Adventure opens
description: The Enhanced Motion Vehicle debuts behind a half-mile themed queue.

title: Indiana Jones Adventure opens at Disneyland
description: Debut of the Enhanced Motion Vehicle, a motion base on a steerable chassis.

title: Flight of Fear opens
description: Premier Rides' twin coasters are the first launched by linear induction motors.

title: Flight of Fear launches with linear induction motors
description: Premier Rides' 44 LIM units push the train to 54 mph in about four seconds, the first LIM-launched coaster.

title: Flight of Fear opens at Kings Island and Kings Dominion
description: First roller coasters launched by linear induction motors, by Premier Rides.

title: Superman: The Escape opens
description: An LSM shuttle reaches 100 mph and 415 ft, the first coaster over 400 ft.

title: Disney's Animal Kingdom opens
description: Joe Rohde's park around the 145 ft Tree of Life.

title: The experience economy is named
description: Pine and Gilmore's Harvard Business Review article.

title: Merlin Entertainments founded
description: Nick Varney's management buyout of Vardon Attractions.

title: Carnegie Mellon Entertainment Technology Center founded
description: Randy Pausch and Don Marinelli create the project-based master's programme that feeds interactive and immersive entertainment careers.

title: Disney introduces FastPass
description: The first large-scale free virtual queue in a theme park, launched late in 1999.

title: Disney introduces FastPass
description: Free timed-return tickets let guests skip the standby line, the first mass-market virtual queue.

title: Islands of Adventure opens with Spider-Man
description: Motion bases on a track plus 3D screens define the media dark ride; Thea Award in 2000.

title: Don Carson publishes 'Environmental Storytelling'
description: An ex-Imagineer carries theme-park storytelling techniques into game level design.

title: Millennium Force opens
description: The first giga coaster, 310 ft, with a cable lift.

title: Millennium Force opens with cable lift and magnetic brakes
description: Intamin's catch-car cable lift climbs 310 ft at 15 mph and eddy-current brakes stop the train from 65 mph in about six seconds.

title: Pooh's Hunny Hunt opens
description: Tokyo Disneyland's trackless dark ride, the system later used in Mystic Manor.

title: Pooh's Hunny Hunt opens at Tokyo Disneyland
description: First full attraction on a sensor-guided trackless ride system.

title: Hypersonic XLC opens
description: S&S's first compressed-air launch coaster.

title: Tokyo DisneySea opens
description: Seven ports of call; 10 million guests in 307 days.

title: Haunted Mansion Holiday debuts at Disneyland
description: The Nightmare Before Christmas overlay opens, becoming the model for annual seasonal re-dressing of a dark ride.

title: Arrow Dynamics files for bankruptcy
description: S&S buys the assets in 2002, ending the company that built the Matterhorn.

title: Xcelerator opens
description: Intamin's first hydraulic launch: 0 to 82 mph in 2.3 seconds.

title: Xcelerator opens as the first hydraulic launch coaster
description: Knott's Berry Farm's Intamin coaster reaches 82 mph in 2.3 seconds using nitrogen accumulators and a winch-driven catch car.

title: John Hench's Designing Disney is published
description: Hench sets down forced perspective, colour and the 'art of the show' in his own words.

title: Top Thrill Dragster opens
description: The first strata coaster, 420 ft and 120 mph.

title: Big Thunder Mountain Railroad derailment at Disneyland
description: A guide wheel comes off a train and the locomotive is forced onto the first car; one guest dies. Maintenance omissions are later acknowledged.

title: Rowling signs a letter of intent with Disney
description: A Harry Potter area for the Magic Kingdom is agreed in principle; Disney later withdraws.

title: Kingda Ka opens
description: 456 ft and 128 mph: the tallest coaster until its 2024 closure.

title: Six Flags New Orleans operates for the last time
description: Hurricane Katrina floods the park eight days later; it never reopens.

title: Hong Kong Disneyland opens
description: A 52/48 government-Disney joint venture designed with feng shui input.

title: Hong Kong Disneyland opens
description: Designed with feng shui advice, including a bend in the entrance walkway.

title: Expedition Everest opens after six years of planning and construction
description: Construction began March 2003; the mountain, coaster and yeti are three independent structures coordinated with 4D scheduling.

title: Expedition Everest opens
description: A $100 million Vekoma coaster with switch tracks and a 25 ft Yeti.

title: The Season Pass podcast launches
description: Doug Barnes starts the show as fan commentary; it grows into an industry forum for attraction creators.

title: Universal announces the Wizarding World
description: A 20-acre Harry Potter land for Islands of Adventure, licensed from Warner Bros.

title: Hard Rock Park opens
description: The Myrtle Beach park files for bankruptcy in September of the same year.

title: World of Color opens at Disney California Adventure
description: More than 1,200 fountains and a 380-foot combined mist screen.

title: Wizarding World of Harry Potter opens
description: Forbidden Journey's KUKA arms debut; Islands of Adventure attendance rises 29% that year.

title: Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey opens
description: KUKA robot arms on a track carry riders through sets and projection domes.

title: Harry Potter and the Forbidden Journey opens
description: Universal's Hogwarts queue becomes the benchmark for queue storytelling.

title: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design issued
description: US standards include sections 234 and 1002 on amusement rides: wheelchair spaces, transfer seats and devices.

title: Formula Rossa opens
description: A 240 km/h hydraulic launch at Ferrari World, the fastest coaster until 2025.

title: Ferrari World Abu Dhabi opens
description: A mostly indoor park under one roof shows how hot-climate sites move the whole park inside.

title: Haunted Mansion interactive queue previews at Magic Kingdom
description: Touch-responsive crypts and instruments turn waiting into play.

title: New Texas Giant reopens
description: The first RMC I-Box conversion of a wooden coaster.

title: Star Tours – The Adventures Continue opens
description: Randomised film segments give about 1,500 different flights, a lever for re-riding.

title: Transformers: The Ride opens in Singapore
description: Oceaneering vehicles with six-axis motion bases; Hollywood and Orlando follow.

title: Disneyland refreshes the Main Street, U.S.A. music loop
description: First change in about twenty years; over a dozen period-style arrangements join the existing loop.

title: Press tour of Imagineering's DISH projection cave
description: Imagineers show how Cars Land and Carthay Circle were walked through at full scale before construction.

title: Disney agrees to buy Lucasfilm
description: A $4.05 billion deal that names theme parks among its uses for Star Wars.

title: Outlaw Run opens with inverting Topper Track
description: Rocky Mountain Construction's steel-topped wooden track carries multiple inversions on a wooden coaster for the first time.

title: Mystic Manor opens
description: Hong Kong Disneyland's trackless manor avoids ghosts for cultural reasons; TEA award in November.

title: WDI's Shanghai castle BIM workflow wins an AIA TAP award
description: Architects on Revit, engineers on AutoCAD, with scripted daily data exchange between Glendale and Shanghai.

title: Chimelong Ocean Kingdom grand opening
description: The Zhuhai park grows to 12.6 million guests by 2024.

title: Diagon Alley opens
description: The second Wizarding World land, linked to Hogsmeade by the Hogwarts Express.

title: ISO 17842-1 first edition published
description: ISO/TC 254 publishes the first international ride design standard, later withdrawn in favour of the 2023 edition.

title: The Hatbox Ghost returns with a projected face
description: The illusion that failed in 1969 under ambient light is rebuilt using projection mapping on the figure.

title: The Smiler collision at Alton Towers
description: A loaded train is released into a stalled empty train after engineers override the block system; several riders are seriously injured.

title: Alpenexpress VR-Ride unveiled at Europa-Park
description: First VR coaster: headsets synced to a 1984 mine train; VR Coaster GmbH founded the same year.

title: Disney moves one-day tickets to date-based tiers
description: Value, Regular and Peak pricing arrives at Disneyland and Walt Disney World.

title: Galactica reopens with VR headsets
description: Alton Towers' flying coaster Air returns with a Gear VR headset at every seat.

title: Shanghai Disneyland opens
description: No Main Street, a Mickey Avenue, and the largest Disney castle.

title: Thunder River Rapids tragedy at Dreamworld
description: A pump failure strands a raft on the conveyor and the following raft collides with it; four people die.

title: Defunctland premieres
description: Kevin Perjurer's documentary series on closed attractions starts on YouTube.

title: Pandora and Flight of Passage open
description: A link-chair flying simulator with 10K 60 fps stereo media.

title: Pandora – The World of Avatar opens
description: A land designed to transform at night, with bioluminescent plants driven by LEDs, fibre optics and blacklight.

title: Symbolica opens at Efteling
description: A EUR 35 million ETF trackless ride with three selectable routes.

title: Fire Ball failure at the Ohio State Fair
description: A gondola arm separates in motion; one rider dies. The manufacturer attributes it to hidden internal corrosion and halts similar rides worldwide.

title: The Void opens Star Wars: Secrets of the Empire
description: Free-walk hyper-reality VR with physical sets launches at Disney Springs; the company closes in 2020.

title: 1,218 drones fly at the Pyeongchang Winter Olympics opening
description: Intel Shooting Star drones set a world record for simultaneous drones, moving drone shows into the mainstream.

title: Sesame Place becomes the first theme park Certified Autism Center
description: IBCCES certification with staff training, a sensory guide and quiet rooms.

title: Steel Vengeance opens
description: Mean Streak becomes the first hyper-hybrid, with four inversions.

title: Stuntronics revealed
description: Disney shows a humanoid stunt-double robot that flips untethered and lands on its mark, following Stickman in May.

title: Warner Bros. World Abu Dhabi opens
description: A fully enclosed, air-conditioned park with six themed areas, later recognised as the world's largest indoor theme park.

title: Galactica's VR headsets removed
description: After a 2018 cut-back to three rows, the park removes VR, citing guest feedback.

title: Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge opens at Disneyland
description: A 14-acre land set on the planet Batuu; Walt Disney World's opens on August 29.

title: Hagrid's Magical Creatures Motorbike Adventure opens
description: Site cleared January 2018, first train installed December 2018, ride testing from February 2019.

title: Imagineering in a Box launches on Khan Academy
description: Walt Disney Imagineering releases a free 32-video course on world-building and attraction design.

title: Rise of the Resistance opens, 14 weeks after its land
description: Disney had announced in March 2019 that the ride would follow as phase two of Galaxy's Edge.

title: Rise of the Resistance opens
description: An 18-minute multi-system ride launched with boarding-group virtual queues.

title: Star Wars: Rise of the Resistance opens
description: A queue, two pre-shows and four ride systems chained into one continuous story.

title: Queensland coroner delivers Dreamworld findings
description: Coroner James McDougall finds no engineering risk assessment was ever done and calls the park's safety systems frighteningly unsophisticated.

title: Imagineering in a Box released
description: Disney Imagineering, Khan Academy and Pixar publish the free three-lesson theme park design course with 32 videos.

title: Walt Disney World closes for the pandemic
description: The resort stays shut until July 11, 2020; Disneyland closes March 14 and reopens April 30, 2021.

title: Magic Kingdom reopens with reservations
description: Phased reopening begins; park entry now requires a dated reservation.

title: Walt Disney World tests facial recognition entry
description: Opt-in trial at Magic Kingdom links faces to random numbers with 30-day deletion; later withdrawn after feedback.

title: Super Nintendo World opens in Osaka
description: The Power-Up Band wristband turns a land into a playable game.

title: Disneyland reopens
description: After more than a year closed, the original park reopens.

title: Disney granted patent for automated rockwork rebar design
description: US11030356B2 turns a 3D rock mesh into numbered rebar chips for assembly.

title: Disney Genie announced
description: Free planner that builds and keeps updating itineraries from guest preferences; paid Genie+ launches alongside.

title: Universal Beijing Resort opens
description: A joint venture 70% owned by a Beijing state enterprise.

title: Disney Genie+ and Lightning Lane launch
description: Paid line-skipping replaces the free FastPass system at Walt Disney World.

title: UCF launches BS in Theme Park and Attraction Management
description: Rosen College's degree starts in Fall 2023, having grown from a 2001 track and a 2020 certificate.

title: ISO 17842-1:2023 second edition published
description: The revised international design standard replaces the 2015 edition.

title: BD-X droids roam Galaxy's Edge daily
description: RL-trained bipedal droids become a daily offering at Disneyland through June 2, 2024.

title: Lightning Lane Multi Pass replaces Genie+
description: Disney renames its paid pass and adds advance booking windows of seven days for resort guests and three for others.

title: Kingda Ka closes
description: The tallest coaster closes; its tower is imploded on February 28, 2025.

title: Universal Epic Universe opens
description: Announced 1 August 2019; construction paused July 2020 to March 2021 during the pandemic.

title: Universal Epic Universe opens
description: Five worlds around Celestial Park, including Super Nintendo World and Ministry of Magic.

title: Universal Epic Universe opens
description: A new hub-and-spoke park: Celestial Park at the centre, four portal worlds, about 110 acres inside a 750-acre site held for expansion.

title: Robotic Olaf debuts at Disneyland Paris
description: A free-walking Olaf trained with reinforcement learning opens in World of Frozen.
